title: Efficient routing and spectrum allocation in arbitrary flex-grid entanglement networks
authors: Zachary Goisman, Matthew L. Stevens, Maxwell Goisman, Taman Truong, Gayane Vardoyan, Don Towsley, Nicholas A. Peters, Nageswara S. V. Rao, Guoliang Xue, Joseph M. Lukens
abstract: As practical quantum networks approach large-scale deployment, the need for efficient user-to-user frequency allocation is increasing, yet current approaches only provide partial solutions to the routing and spectrum allocation problem for an arbitrary quantum network. We address this challenge for repeater-less flex-grid quantum networks based on hyperentangled photons using an efficient three-stage pipeline combining leading tools in classical networking with recent advances in numerical optimization. First, double instantiations of Yen's algorithm obtain low-loss route candidates between each pair of users and the entanglement sources. Second, the advanced process optimizer (APOPT) obtains frequency channel allocations that maximize distribution rates under fidelity constraints. Finally, the constraint programming solver using satisfiability methods (CP-SAT) assigns specific frequency bins to each link, ensuring that there is no contention between frequencies from different sources. We numerically demonstrate this approach on a representative ring network and a Manhattan incumbent local exchange carrier topology, realizing significant improvements over prior genetic algorithm approaches in speed, accuracy, and scalability. Overall, this pipeline provides an efficient heuristic workflow for optimizing broadband entanglement distribution, applicable to arbitrarily connected quantum networks integrated within the existing lightwave infrastructure.
summary: This paper presents an efficient, three-stage pipeline to solve the complex routing and spectrum allocation problem in large-scale quantum networks using hyperentangled photons. By combining classical optimization tools like Yen's algorithm, APOPT, and CP-SAT, the authors achieve significant improvements in speed and accuracy over previous methods. This workflow offers a practical heuristic for deploying broadband entanglement distribution across existing fiber optic infrastructure.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently allocating frequency spectrum and routing entanglement links for large-scale, repeater-less quantum networks.
main_result: A novel three-stage heuristic pipeline was developed that significantly outperforms prior genetic algorithm methods in speed and accuracy for optimizing broadband entanglement distribution.
method: The approach combines Yen's algorithm for pathfinding, the Advanced Process Optimizer (APOPT) for rate maximization under fidelity constraints, and a CP-SAT solver for contention-free frequency bin assignment.
model_or_system: The model describes an arbitrary quantum network using hyperentangled photons in a flex-grid WDM setup. Links are characterized by fidelity ($F_\ell$) and coincidence rates ($R_\ell$), which depend on allocated frequencies and optical losses.
key_observables: Fidelity ($F_\ell$), total coincidence rate ($R_\ell$), network utility ($U$), and solution runtime.
important_parameters: Source flux ($\mu_{m\ell}$), optical losses ($\eta_{A\ell}, \eta_{B\ell}$), and the number of available frequency bins ($K$).
main_assumptions: The model assumes that channel distortion effects are fully compensated, and it focuses on the resource allocation aspects applicable to existing lightwave infrastructure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the hardware components (WSSs) and detail the three-stage pipeline: pathfinding (Double Yen), spectrum optimization (APOPT), and frequency scheduling (CP-SAT) applied to example topologies like ring or Manhattan networks.
paper_structure: The paper is structured around defining the NP-hard Quantum Resource Allocation problem, proposing a novel three-stage heuristic pipeline (Route Finding $ightarrow$ Spectrum Allocation $ightarrow$ Bin Assignment), and validating this workflow on representative network topologies.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the engineering bottleneck of scaling quantum networks by providing a computationally efficient framework for resource management in existing optical infrastructure.
